mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market, boosting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is likely to drive corporate earnings and thus S&P 500 returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases by more than 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions or weakening demand, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening housing market and consumer confidence, which is likely to boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% month-over-month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of other economic indicators.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.
